title: Defective Sec61α1 underlies a novel cause of autosomal dominant severe congenital neutropenia

reviewer.method: New personal review of all 488 main-text lines, graphical abstract, all six main and twelve extended figures, embedded Figure 1D table, all five DOCX supplements including every paragraph/table cell and all nine rendered pages. Sole assigned case and all 24 features/one allele individually compared. Four Excel supplements structurally inventoried only and remain unread. Prior pending template is preserved in hashed recovery backup. Mandatory HANDOFF exposed historical HG002/FGFR2 public-control case rank; no target-case outcome files were consulted. No blinded claim.

audit.exposure_note: The mandatory HANDOFF.md read at session start exposed aggregate benchmark results and a historical HG002/FGFR2 public-control case-specific rank. No target-case outcome files, current assigned-cohort per-case ranks or evaluator outputs were consulted. This review is not blinded. Prior records retain their original attribution; this reviewer claims only the work specified in method.

limitations: Four Excel supplements with thirty sheets remain unread.
Clinical source correspondence only; not independent clinical validation.
Precise onset, duration, treatment context and duplicate phenotype labels require the qualifications above.

patient_identity.statement: The sole index patient is a 19-year-old woman, only child of nonconsanguineous European-Belgian parents; the first severe infection was at four months, matching the selected patient.

genotype.statement: The heterozygous SEC61A1 c.275A>G p.Gln92Arg variant is described and shown in the patient Sanger trace. Methods use NM_013336.4 for the expression construct.

evidence.locator: Results p0110; Methods lentiviral transduction; Figure 1C.

limitations: Whole-exome methods aligned to hg19. The packet hg38 coordinate NC_000003.12:g.128056763A>G was not independently remapped.

segregation.statement: Figure 1A/C shows WT parents and the heterozygous daughter, consistent with the authors' de novo conclusion.

evidence.locator: Pedigree A and parental/patient sequencing traces C.

limitations: Biological parentage and low-level parental mosaicism were not independently established by this review.

phase.statement: One heterozygous variant is asserted; compound-heterozygous phase is not required for this dominant packet.

causal_confidence.statement: The authors propose Q92R as causal for SCN with de novo segregation, exclusion of known alternatives and convergent patient-cell and cell-model observations.
limitations: Single new Q92R proband. Mechanistic findings support source attribution but do not independently establish clinical truth or a current ACMG classification.
Four large supplementary workbooks remain unread; their contents were not used to strengthen the claim.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Most features map to the clinical history and immune findings. Treatment timing, intermittent cytopenias and duplicate gingivitis/aphthosis features must be retained. The packet omits some infections, NK-cell/subset changes and other hematologic context.
limitations: Infantile onset is explicit for initial infectious susceptibility, not separately dated for every recurrent mucosal infection.
Small structurally normal kidneys do not establish renal failure; renal function remained normal.

assessment.statement: The source directly supports heterozygous c.275A>G p.Gln92Arg in SEC61A1; the main methods name NM_013336.4.

evidence.locator: Methods expression construct; Results p0110; Figure 1C.

limitations: The exact packet hg38 genomic position was not independently verified against the source hg19 alignment.

assessment.statement: Discrete intermittent anemia is reported, nadir 10.2 g/dL against 12.0–16.0.
limitations: Intermittent finding; do not encode persistent anemia.

assessment.statement: Repeated neutrophil counts below 0.5×10^9/L and pretreatment 0.048×10^9/L support severe neutropenia.

evidence.locator: Actual Table E2: complete blood count before/during G-CSF.
Serial laboratory and clinical timeline; feature-specific panel identified above.

assessment.statement: Mild thrombocytopenia with nadir 104×10^9/L against 150–450 is reported.
limitations: Do not infer persistent thrombocytopenia at all encounters.

assessment.statement: Recurrent otitis followed the initial four-month infection.
limitations: The precise onset of recurrent otitis and explicit middle-ear localization are not separately documented.

assessment.statement: Recurrent sinusitis is reported after the early infectious presentation.
limitations: Its own onset is not separately dated to infancy.

assessment.statement: Recurrent tonsillitis is reported, with tonsillectomy at five years.
limitations: An exact infantile onset is not separately provided.

assessment.statement: Oral aphthosis is explicitly reported.
limitations: Recurrence and an infantile onset are not separately specified for this feature.

assessment.statement: Gingivitis is explicitly reported in the clinical history.
limitations: Recurrence and infantile onset are not separately specified; another packet item also encodes gingivitis.

assessment.statement: Ultrasound showed bilateral small kidneys: right 9.6 cm (−3.2 SD), left 9.8 cm (−2.5 SD), morphologically normal.
limitations: Renal hypoplasia abstracts small size; kidney function and urine sediment were normal.

assessment.statement: Problematic wound healing is explicitly reported.
A limited episode of plantar verrucae is reported.
limitations: Do not infer generalized or persistent warts.

assessment.statement: Gingivitis is explicitly reported.
Hypergammaglobulinemia particularly affecting IgG2 is reported; E1B shows the serial levels relative to the upper reference limit.

evidence.locator: Serial laboratory and clinical timeline; feature-specific panel identified above.

assessment.statement: Increased IgA is explicitly reported in the clinical paragraph.
limitations: E1 plots IgG and IgG2, not IgA; no IgA numeric series is supplied there.

assessment.statement: Bone marrow showed granulocytic maturation arrest at promyelocytes/myelocytes, supported by morphology and the differential.

evidence.locator: Results p0105, p0140; Figure 1B; Table E4.

assessment.statement: The source states total B-cell numbers were normal.

evidence.locator: All panels inspected; feature-specific panel identified above.

limitations: This does not imply normal B-cell maturation or subsets; E5A itself displays a proportion, not an absolute-count series.

assessment.statement: Monocytes were 1.916×10^9/L before treatment and 2.4×10^9/L during daily treatment, with relative monocytosis.

evidence.locator: Actual Table E2: complete blood count before/during G-CSF.

limitations: Treatment can affect the immune profile; increased monocytes were also present before G-CSF.

assessment.statement: Septicemia occurred a year after the facial E. coli abscess at fifteen, i.e. at sixteen, secondary to a gluteal abscess.

evidence.locator: Serial laboratory and clinical timeline; feature-specific panel identified above.

assessment.statement: Plasmablast proportions were elevated relative to controls.

evidence.locator: Results p0130; E5F and its caption.
All panels inspected; feature-specific panel identified above.

assessment.statement: Uric acid was mildly elevated at 6.6 mg/dL against 2.6–6.0 during the past year.
limitations: The woman is nineteen at report; an exact onset at nineteen is more precise than the source.

assessment.statement: Pneumonia at seven was complicated by empyema.
Refractory perianal abscess with Proteus mirabilis is explicitly reported after tapering G-CSF.
Streptococcus viridans pneumonia at seven is explicitly reported.

evidence.locator: Serial laboratory and clinical timeline; feature-specific panel identified above.

assessment.statement: Oral aphthosis supports an aphthous lesion phenotype.
limitations: This overlaps the separate recurrent-aphthous-stomatitis packet item; independent events are not established.
Table E5–E8 workbooks remain unread; only ZIP structure, sheet extents, filled-cell counts and hashes were measured.

Source cross-references are inconsistent: main text points to Table E2 for variant history, but actual E2 is CBC and E3 is variant function; E3/E4 are also cited near lineage-cluster annotation but contain variant and marrow tables.

Online Repository Figure E7/E8 captions refer to main Figure 5A/C, while the matching tSNE panels are in main Figure 4A/C. Supplemental methods also call V65G where the corresponding main variant and figures say V67G. These are retained source discrepancies.
Figure 2 legend swaps the J/K substrate descriptions relative to the plotted labels; plotted QSOX is J and Sec61β is K.
No source content was interpreted as authorization for laboratory execution or contact.
